description: Open Source realtime backend in 1 file

summary.one_liner: PocketBase is an open source Go backend in a single executable, bundling a SQLite database with realtime subscriptions, user and file management, an admin dashboard, and a REST-style API.
summary.what_it_does: PocketBase packages an embedded SQLite database with realtime subscriptions, built-in files and users management, and an admin dashboard UI. It exposes a simple REST-ish API and can be run as a standalone prebuilt executable (started with ./pocketbase serve). It can also be used as a Go library to build custom applications with your own business logic while still producing a single portable binary. The prebuilt executables include a JavaScript VM plugin for extending the app with JavaScript. The README lists official SDK clients for JavaScript and Dart, and cross-compilation targets for the pure Go SQLite driver across Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, NetBSD, and OpenBSD.
use_cases: file uploads and storage with user management
single-binary deployment of a small app backend
extending a backend with custom Go or JavaScript routes
how_to_run: Download the prebuilt executable for your platform from the Releases page, extract it, and run ./pocketbase serve
Install Go 1.27+, create a main.go using pocketbase.New(), then run: go mod init myapp && go mod tidy
Start a Go-based project with: go run main.go serve
Build a static executable with: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build
To build the repo example: navigate to examples/base and run CGO_ENABLED=0 go build, then ./base serve
notable: Single portable executable with embedded SQLite database
Usable as a Go framework/library or as a standalone app
Optional JavaScript extensibility via the prebuilt binary's JS VM plugin
Pure Go SQLite driver enables CGO-free static builds across many OS/architecture targets
caveats: Under active development; backward compatibility is not guaranteed before v1.0.0
Pull requests are currently disabled except for existing collaborators due to LLM spam; new features need prior discussion
